fDiJNfDOrDc.title: Activism, Our Path Forward 3: Our Compassion and Clarity
fDiJNfDOrDc.one_line: From the cave youths' prayer for mercy and right guidance: activists need compassion for those not yet awake and clear, agreed goals before next steps.
fDiJNfDOrDc.summary: After October 7 people are finally listening, and he turns again to the youths of the cave, who asked Allah for mercy and for right guidance in their affair. These are the two things an activist needs. First, compassion: the great pitfall of anyone who gains moral clarity is to judge and turn harsh toward those who have not, as people newly returned to practice often do with parents, spouses and children. Hold yourself to the standard but be merciful with others; everyone rides a noisy train that stops for each at a different time, and no one gave more than the Prophet, yet he did not judge. Second, clarity of direction: nobody knows the exact next step, so Muslims must work as a group, accept mistakes and sometimes go with the majority as the Prophet did. The cave's 'raqim' was a written record of vision and values, and his community has no defined goals; more facilities is not a goal, and without a destination no map can give directions. In the second khutbah he quotes Ibn al-Qayyim on the hardships of the prophets' path, retells Ta'if, where the Prophet refused to have his persecutors destroyed, and the charity of Abu Bakr and Umar, arguing that a dedicated life is also a happier one.

outline.heading: Opening
After October 7, people are listening
outline.gist: Muslims could never afford silence, even before October 7, but no one was listening; after months of what Gaza has endured, people are listening again, so this has to be said in English and said properly.

outline.heading: The youths' prayer: mercy and right guidance
outline.gist: Continuing from last week's talk on youth: the youths took refuge in the cave and asked, 'Our Lord, give us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us right guidance in our affair', and were promised that their Lord would spread His mercy and ease their matter.

outline.heading: The first pitfall: judging those without your clarity
outline.gist: Since October 7 many Muslims have realized Islam is far more than rituals and culture; with the clutter removed they see the simplicity of why we are here. The biggest pitfall of anyone who gains moral clarity is failing to understand why others do not see it, then judging them and becoming harsh.

outline.heading: You did not want to be judged either
outline.gist: You did not want people putting you under a microscope before your eyes opened, so keep giving others compassion. Activists who become hateful toward those who do not match their dedication have fallen into the number one pitfall.

outline.heading: Harsh with family after returning to practice
outline.gist: He sees it constantly: someone returns to practice and becomes harsh with parents, siblings, spouse and children. Hold yourself to the standard you have found, but be merciful toward those who have not arrived yet.

outline.heading: Everyone's train stops at a different time
outline.gist: Life is a noisy train that stops at different times for each person, and only at a stop can you step back and revise yourself. The person you are judging may not have reached their stop, and their sense of where time and wealth should go may differ from yours.

outline.heading: Hate holds activists back; the Prophet judged no one
outline.gist: Hatred makes it hard to reach out and help people along their way. No one dedicated more of his life than the Prophet, yet he did not judge people for where they were; he saw the good in them and amplified it.

outline.heading: What next? Nobody knows, so move as a group
outline.gist: 'Prepare for us right guidance in our affair' is the everlasting question of what to do next for the cause. No one here knows the exact sequence of steps; there are only opinions, so we must work as a group, accept that we will make mistakes and fail, and move with the group even when it goes another way.

outline.heading: No one knows for sure: even the Prophet went with the majority
outline.gist: Those without flexibility and openness fail, and acting as if you know for certain is unhealthy. The Prophet made decisions that did not always work, went with the majority opinion to fight outside the city, and never pointed fingers when it went wrong.

outline.heading: The raqim: a written vision and values
outline.gist: The raqim was a document where the youths wrote down their vision, mission, principles and values, and it guided those who carried on their revolution after they disappeared. What do we as a community want to achieve?

outline.heading: No destination, no directions
outline.gist: We cannot discuss next steps until the community defines what it wants to achieve in ten years. Your phone's maps cannot tell you to turn right or left without a destination.

outline.heading: More facilities is not a goal; the two things an activist needs
outline.gist: More spaces and facilities is not a goal. An activist who understands Islam as the Prophet and the Quran present it needs two things: compassion for those not yet where you are, and knowing where you are going.

outline.heading: Interlude
The seerah is effort: the path that wearied the prophets
outline.gist: The seerah is not a string of events but the effort the Prophet gave until he met his Lord. Ibn al-Qayyim: 'O you of weak resolve', this is the path that wearied Adam, made Nuh weep, put Ibrahim in the fire and saw Zakariyya sawn; you will not win it through play. Since October 7, people have come to imams everywhere seeking answers.

outline.heading: Mercy for those still at play
outline.gist: The injustice spread in the world has finally reached people and their sacred places; better late than never. The first need is mercy: do not judge or look down on those still at play, because Allah enlightened your sight by His grace.

outline.heading: Right guidance: agree on the goal before the steps
outline.gist: You were once the person at play; if you cannot help him, be merciful, since harming him is audacity before Allah. The second need is right guidance: Muslims in the West and across the Arab and Muslim world must agree on their goals first, because without a qiblah it makes no difference whether you turn right or left.

outline.heading: I'm already on the ship
outline.gist: If you have not agreed to be an activist, that is your problem: he is already on the ship. Reality changes only when a population takes responsibility for changing it, as every prophet and companion did, starting young and belonging to the group.

outline.heading: Ta'if: perhaps from their descendants
outline.gist: Humiliated, barred from Makkah with daughters at home, he was offered the angel of the mountains to crush Quraysh between the two mountains. He refused, hoping Allah would bring from their descendants people who say la ilaha illa Allah, 'and here we are'. Truly spoke the One who named him kind and merciful.

outline.heading: A cause worth everything: Umar's half and Abu Bakr's all
outline.gist: Activism is a cause so meaningful you would give up all you own. Umar brought half his wealth thinking he would surpass Abu Bakr, who brought everything and left his family Allah and His Messenger; Umar knew he would never outdo him. He is not asking them to do the same.

outline.heading: A dedicated life is a happier one
outline.gist: Only a dedicated life puts its wealth behind the cause, and that is how the companions lived. Living this way you are healthier, happier and more productive, not deprived of fun or relationships.

outline.heading: What saved them will save us
outline.gist: Because the early Muslims lived this way, people of every background could accept Islam; without it Islam would not have reached us. The next generation cannot sit back: what saved them will save us.

outline.heading: Outro

65:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وَأَحۡصُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّكُمۡۖ لَا تُخۡرِجُوهُنَّ مِنۢ بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلَا يَخۡرُجۡنَ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةࣲ مُّبَيِّنَةࣲۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ ظَلَمَ نَفۡسَهُۥۚ لَا تَدۡرِي لَعَلَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحۡدِثُ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ أَمۡرࣰ ا
65:1.en: O Prophet! When ye (men) put away women, put them away for their (legal) period and reckon the period, and keep your duty to Allah, your Lord. Expel them not from their houses nor let them go forth unless they commit open immorality. Such are the limits (imposed by) Allah; and whoso transgresseth Allah's limits, he verily wrongeth his soul. Thou knowest not: it may be that Allah will afterward bring some new thing to pass

65:2.ar: فَإِذَا بَلَغۡنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمۡسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ فَارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفࣲ وَأَشۡهِدُواْ ذَوَيۡ عَدۡلࣲ مِّنكُمۡ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلشَّهَٰدَةَ لِلَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ يُوعَظُ بِهِۦ مَن كَانَ يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ مَخۡرَجࣰ ا
65:2.en: Then, when they have reached their term, take them back in kindness or part from them in kindness, and call to witness two just men among you, and keep your testimony upright for Allah. Whoso believeth in Allah and the Last Day is exhorted to act thus. And whosoever keepeth his duty to Allah, Allah will appoint a way out for him

2:229.ar: ٱلطَّلَٰقُ مَرَّتَانِۖ فَإِمۡسَاكُۢ بِمَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ تَسۡرِيحُۢ بِإِحۡسَٰنࣲۗ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَأۡخُذُواْ مِمَّآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِۖ فَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفۡتَدَتۡ بِهِۦۗ تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَعۡتَدُوهَاۚ وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
2:229.en: Divorce must be pronounced twice and then (a woman) must be retained in honour or released in kindness. And it is not lawful for you that ye take from women aught of that which ye have given them; except (in the case) when both fear that they may not be able to keep within the limits (imposed by) Allah. And if ye fear that they may not be able to keep the limits of Allah, in that case it is no sin for either of them if the woman ransom herself. These are the limits (imposed by) Allah. Transgress them not. For whoso transgresseth Allah's limits: such are wrong-doers

oopv3SR8XN0.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Talaq, Part 1 (65:1-2)
oopv3SR8XN0.one_line: Introducing Surat Al-Talaq: removing the stigma of divorce, why it must be regulated, the waiting period's wisdom, and ending marriages with goodness.
oopv3SR8XN0.summary: He opens Al-Talaq with a long introduction on how Muslims have lost the balance around marriage and divorce. Divorce is disliked and deeply stressful, but it is an admission of failure like any other, and treating it as a shameful scar leads people either to hide or to blame the other spouse entirely instead of learning. He links this to oversized weddings, late marriage, double standards between sons and daughters, and suspicion of divorcees, pointing to the companions who divorced and remarried easily and to the Prophet's marriage to Khadijah. Turning to verse 1, he notes that the Prophet, who never divorced, is addressed before a plural command, which shows divorce must be overseen by leadership and courts; he argues Muslims need their own civil courts that hold men to their greater responsibility. He explains divorcing only in a state of purity without intercourse, counting the waiting period carefully, and the wife staying in the home while the husband leaves so both can reflect, since Allah may bring about something new. He also explains 'isma, control of the marriage. On verse 2 he insists couples either stay together or part with goodness, entering and leaving with respect, because children are harmed by parental hostility more than by a respectful divorce.

outline.heading: From Al-Munafiqun back to organizing society
outline.gist: After the reminder to remember why we act, the cluster returns to organization with the domestic relationship and how marriage ends.

outline.heading: Divorce as a religious and cultural taboo
outline.gist: Divorce had long been taboo, absent in Catholic teaching and restricted in Jewish tradition, and in pre-Islamic Arabia its shame made marriages oppressive to women.

outline.heading: Disliked but not shameful
outline.gist: Islam does not encourage divorce, one of the most stressful experiences a person can have, but when needed it should happen justly and leave no stain.

outline.heading: Divorce as an admission of failure no one cares about
outline.gist: Divorce admits the marriage did not work, and nobody outside close family wants the details; we are not that important.

outline.heading: Why is failing a marriage worse than other failures?
outline.gist: Shame pushes people into self-righteous blame of the other spouse, though almost no divorce is entirely one person's fault.

outline.heading: Muslim divorce rates now match everyone else's
outline.gist: Muslims once took pride in holding families together by getting over their egos; now rates mirror the wider society.

outline.heading: Take your share of the blame and learn
outline.gist: Like a failed business blamed entirely on others, a divorce teaches nothing unless one owns part of the failure.

outline.heading: Oversized weddings make failure unadmittable
outline.gist: Endless hoops and lavish multi-night weddings, unknown to the Prophet and companions, make it nearly impossible to admit a marriage is not working.

outline.heading: Companions divorced and remarried often
outline.gist: The waiting period partly exists because divorced women had suitors lining up; today divorcees face suspicion as if the other family's son were flawless.

outline.heading: Everyone is flawed: the pizza box
outline.gist: Unless a person is abusive or pathologically dishonest, the next person will just have different flaws, so do not discard a reasonable match.

outline.heading: The balance: fight for the marriage, then part without scars
outline.gist: Work hard to keep the union, but if it fails, divorce should allow both to remarry; the second time is easier because one learns.

outline.heading: Experience, not a stain: Khadijah's previous marriages
outline.gist: A divorcee brings experience; the Prophet loved Khadijah, twice married before, above everyone and cared for her children.

outline.heading: Polygamy is not the fix; double standards are the problem
outline.gist: Fathers who want reasonable terms for their sons become unreasonable for their daughters, as if their daughter were uniquely precious.

outline.heading: An epidemic of late marriage
outline.gist: Practising men and women in their thirties who have never married were almost unheard of when people were starving, yet still married simply.

outline.heading: Four imbalances and vicious endings
outline.gist: Marriage is too expensive and too late, divorce too frequent and too scarring; marriages must not end in hatred that destroys reputations.

outline.heading: Spiritual verses amid technical surahs
outline.gist: The surah opens by addressing the Prophet and, like other legal passages, places some of the Quran's most beautiful verses among technical rulings.

outline.heading: Interlude
Addressed to the Prophet, who never divorced
outline.gist: The Prophet is always called by his title; there is no authentic report that he ever divorced, only a month's vow of separation he ended early.

outline.heading: Divorce must be regulated by leadership
outline.gist: Calling on the Prophet and then using the plural shows divorce needs a standard, a judiciary and a role model, not just private compliance.

outline.heading: The case for Muslim civil courts
outline.gist: Civil law treats marriage as fifty-fifty, but in Islam the man carries more responsibility; Muslim judges could prevent divorces by holding men to it.

outline.heading: Elders and guardians as the woman's insurance
outline.gist: A man answerable to his father, uncles and elders protects his wife; the families at a nikah stand as guarantors of good conduct.

outline.heading: A structure that makes people behave
outline.gist: A proper court tells the party at fault to smarten up; he holds a woman is better off in a properly run Islamic court than a secular one.

outline.heading: Perceived unfairness breeds resentment
outline.gist: Lasting marriages are those where each spouse feels the other carries their weight; unrealistic expectations must be addressed before marriage.

outline.heading: Divorce only in a state of purity without relations
outline.gist: Divorcing during menstruation, or after intimacy in that cycle, is forbidden; this forces a delay of ten to fifteen days and protects her from feeling used.

outline.heading: Count the waiting period carefully; the first call to taqwa
outline.gist: The three cycles must be counted precisely, and this is the first of the surah's repeated calls to taqwa.

outline.heading: Allah, your Lord: majesty and nearness
outline.gist: Pairing the name Allah with Rabb joins a name of majesty that brings awe and a name of care that brings compassion.

outline.heading: How he presents the rulings
outline.gist: He gives the majority opinions of the schools and notes which he finds more valid today, rather than following one madhhab.

outline.heading: She stays in the home; he leaves
outline.gist: During the waiting period the wife may not be removed from the home or move out, and the husband leaves and pays the rent.

outline.heading: Why: he feels the loss, she processes
outline.gist: Losing his home makes him appreciate what he had, while staying lets her grieve and face what she wants to run from, so both can reconsider.

outline.heading: Going back to her family is not Islamic
outline.gist: The setup aims to preserve marriages; the only exception is clear indecency committed in the home.

outline.heading: The boundaries of Allah
outline.gist: The verse previews the surah's rulings; before Islam men divorced at any time and threw women out, sometimes stranded far from family.

outline.heading: Whoever oversteps them wrongs himself
outline.gist: A direct warning to anyone who treats Allah's limits as not worth observing.

outline.heading: Perhaps Allah will bring about a new matter
outline.gist: A phrase that became a proverb: during the waiting period things may change, and following Allah's rules leaves room for what He prepares.

outline.heading: After the waiting period: reconcile or remarry
outline.gist: Within the period the husband can take her back; after it a new contract is needed, and after a third divorce they cannot remarry unless she marries someone else.

outline.heading: 'Isma: who controls the marriage
outline.gist: By default the man holds control over whether the marriage continues, reflecting his greater responsibility, which is why an Islamic court serves women.

outline.heading: The sheikh who sent a complaining student away
outline.gist: When a student complained endlessly about his wife, his teacher told him to divorce her or persevere, a lesson on a husband's responsibility he witnessed at fourteen.

outline.heading: Someone must pilot the ship
outline.gist: 'Isma can be given to the wife and sometimes is removed from temper-driven men, but Islamic marriage requires someone to hold it.

outline.heading: Interlude
Reaching the end of the term
outline.gist: When the waiting period ends, one of two outcomes must follow.

outline.heading: Hold on with ma'ruf
outline.gist: Ma'ruf is what society recognizes as good within Islamic values; staying married must be with kindness, not spite or resentment.

outline.heading: Or part with ma'ruf

outline.heading: Leave as you entered

outline.heading: The command least obeyed

outline.heading: Children are harmed by hostility, not by divorce

28:38.ar: وَقَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡمَلَأُ مَا عَلِمۡتُ لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرِي فَأَوۡقِدۡ لِي يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلطِّينِ فَٱجۡعَل لِّي صَرۡحࣰ ا لَّعَلِّيٓ أَطَّلِعُ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
28:38.en: And Pharaoh said: O chiefs! I know not that ye have a god other than me, so kindle for me (a fire), O Haman, to bake the mud; and set up for me a lofty tower in order that I may survey the god of Moses; and lo! I deem him of the liars

28:39.ar: وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ هُوَ وَجُنُودُهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡنَا لَا يُرۡجَعُونَ
28:39.en: And he and his hosts were haughty in the land without right, and deemed that they would never be brought back to Us

28:40.ar: فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّۖ فَٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
28:40.en: Therefor We seized him and his hosts, and abandoned them unto the sea. Behold the nature of the consequence for evil-doers

28:41.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمۡ أَئِمَّةࣰ يَدۡعُونَ إِلَى ٱلنَّارِۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
28:41.en: And We made them patterns that invite unto the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped

28:42.ar: وَأَتۡبَعۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعۡنَةࣰۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ هُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمَقۡبُوحِينَ
28:42.en: And We made a curse to follow them in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the hateful

28:43.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَهۡلَكۡنَا ٱلۡقُرُونَ ٱلۡأُولَىٰ بَصَآئِرَ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدࣰ ى وَرَحۡمَةࣰ لَّعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
28:43.en: And We verily gave the Scripture unto Moses after We had destroyed the generations of old: clear testimonies for mankind, and a guidance and a mercy, that haply they might reflect

28:44.ar: وَمَا كُنتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلۡغَرۡبِيِّ إِذۡ قَضَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلۡأَمۡرَ وَمَا كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
28:44.en: And thou (Muhammad) wast not on the western side (of the Mount) when We expounded unto Moses the commandment, and thou wast not among those present

43:54.ar: فَٱسۡتَخَفَّ قَوۡمَهُۥ فَأَطَاعُوهُۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
43:54.en: Thus he persuaded his people to make light (of Moses), and they obeyed him. Lo! they were a wanton folk

43:81.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَلَدࣱ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡعَٰبِدِينَ
43:81.en: Say (O Muhammad): If the Beneficent One hath a son, then, I shall be first among the worshippers. (But there is no son)

2:258.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِي حَآجَّ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ فِي رَبِّهِۦٓ أَنۡ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ إِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّيَ ٱلَّذِي يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا۠ أُحۡيِۦ وَأُمِيتُۖ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡتِي بِٱلشَّمۡسِ مِنَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ فَأۡتِ بِهَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ فَبُهِتَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَرَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:258.en: Bethink thee of him who had an argument with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him the kingdom; how, when Abraham said: My Lord is He Who giveth life and causeth death, he answered: I give life and cause death. Abraham said: Lo! Allah causeth the sun to rise in the East, so do thou cause it to come up from the West. Thus was the disbeliever abashed. And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

20:47.ar: فَأۡتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرۡسِلۡ مَعَنَا بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡۖ قَدۡ جِئۡنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكَۖ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ
20:47.en: So go ye unto him and say: Lo! we are two messengers of thy Lord. So let the children of Israel go with us, and torment them not. We bring thee a token from thy Lord. And peace will be for him who followeth right guidance

26:62.ar: قَالَ كَلَّآۖ إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهۡدِينِ
26:62.en: He said: Nay, verily! for lo! my Lord is with me. He will guide me

26:63.ar: فَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَۖ فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرۡقࣲ كَٱلطَّوۡدِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
26:63.en: Then We inspired Moses, saying: Smite the sea with thy staff. And it parted, and each part was as a mountain vast

2:124.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتࣲ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّۖ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامࣰ اۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِيۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهۡدِي ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:124.en: And (remember) when his Lord tried Abraham with (His) commands, and he fulfilled them, He said: Lo! I have appointed thee a leader for mankind. (Abraham) said: And of my offspring (will there be leaders)? He said: My covenant includeth not wrong-doers

11:98.ar: يَقۡدُمُ قَوۡمَهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ فَأَوۡرَدَهُمُ ٱلنَّارَۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡوِرۡدُ ٱلۡمَوۡرُودُ
11:98.en: He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them to the Fire for watering-place. Ah, hapless is the watering-place (whither they are) led

16:25.ar: لِيَحۡمِلُوٓاْ أَوۡزَارَهُمۡ كَامِلَةࣰ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَمِنۡ أَوۡزَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُم بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمٍۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَزِرُونَ
16:25.en: That they may bear their burdens undiminished on the Day of Resurrection, with somewhat of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Ah! evil is that which they bear

86:13.en: Lo! this (Qur'an) is a conclusive word

10:83.ar: فَمَآ ءَامَنَ لِمُوسَىٰٓ إِلَّا ذُرِّيَّةࣱ مِّن قَوۡمِهِۦ عَلَىٰ خَوۡفࣲ مِّن فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِمۡ أَن يَفۡتِنَهُمۡۚ وَإِنَّ فِرۡعَوۡنَ لَعَالࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡرِفِينَ
10:83.en: But none trusted Moses, save some scions of his people, (and they were) in fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs, that he would persecute them. Lo! Pharaoh was verily a tyrant in the land, and lo! he verily was of the wanton

26:14.ar: وَلَهُمۡ عَلَيَّ ذَنۢبࣱ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقۡتُلُونِ
26:14.en: And they have a crime against me, so I fear that they will kill me

20:44.ar: فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوۡلࣰ ا لَّيِّنࣰ ا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوۡ يَخۡشَىٰ
20:44.en: And speak unto him a gentle word, that peradventure he may heed or fear

79:18.ar: فَقُلۡ هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ
79:18.en: And say (unto him): Hast thou (will) to grow (in grace)

79:19.en: Then I will guide thee to thy Lord and thou shalt fear (Him)

18:10.ar: إِذۡ أَوَى ٱلۡفِتۡيَةُ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحۡمَةࣰ وَهَيِّئۡ لَنَا مِنۡ أَمۡرِنَا رَشَدࣰ ا
18:10.en: When the young men fled for refuge to the Cave and said: Our Lord! Give us mercy from Thy presence, and shape for us right conduct in our plight

7:172.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَأَشۡهَدَهُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ أَلَسۡتُ بِرَبِّكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ شَهِدۡنَآۚ أَن تَقُولُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنۡ هَٰذَا غَٰفِلِينَ
7:172.en: And (remember) when thy Lord brought forth from the Children of Adam, from their reins, their seed, and made them testify of themselves, (saying): Am I not your Lord? They said: Yea, verily. We testify. (That was) lest ye should say at the Day of Resurrection: Lo! of this we were unaware

28:29.ar: ۞فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلۡأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهۡلِهِۦٓ ءَانَسَ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ نَارࣰ اۖ قَالَ لِأَهۡلِهِ ٱمۡكُثُوٓاْ إِنِّيٓ ءَانَسۡتُ نَارࣰ ا لَّعَلِّيٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنۡهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوۡ جَذۡوَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَصۡطَلُونَ
28:29.en: Then, when Moses had fulfilled the term, and was travelling with his housefolk, he saw in the distance a fire and said unto his housefolk: Bide ye (here). Lo! I see in the distance a fire; peradventure I shall bring you tidings thence, or a brand from the fire that ye may warm yourselves

28:30.ar: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِيَ مِن شَٰطِيِٕ ٱلۡوَادِ ٱلۡأَيۡمَنِ فِي ٱلۡبُقۡعَةِ ٱلۡمُبَٰرَكَةِ مِنَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ أَن يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّيٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
28:30.en: And when he reached it, he was called from the right side of the valley in the blessed field, from the tree: O Moses! Lo! I, even I, am Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

28:31.ar: وَأَنۡ أَلۡقِ عَصَاكَۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهۡتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنࣱّ وَلَّىٰ مُدۡبِرࣰ ا وَلَمۡ يُعَقِّبۡۚ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقۡبِلۡ وَلَا تَخَفۡۖ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓمِنِينَ
28:31.en: Throw down thy staff. And when he saw it writhing as it had been a demon, he turned to flee headlong, (and it was said unto him): O Moses! Draw nigh and fear not. Lo! thou art of those who are secure

J4gsVOzJKZQ.title: Arabic Tafsir of Surat al-Qasas: Pharaoh's Fallacies and His Fate, Verses 38-44
J4gsVOzJKZQ.one_line: Pharaoh's straw man and stalling, then arrogance, leading people to the fire, a lasting curse, guidance with mercy, and 'you were not there'.
J4gsVOzJKZQ.summary: Picking up from verse 38, the sheikh names Pharaoh's tactics as logical fallacies everyone should learn: the loaded question atheists pose about a stone too heavy to lift, the straw man of claiming Musa said his Lord could be seen from a tower, arguing against conclusions you assume someone's words imply, which he says drives sectarian and marital disputes alike, and prolonging a problem until attention dies, as with Gaza. Truth needs no loud claims, only space to be presented. Verses 39-42 then name Pharaoh's crimes: arrogance, which contradicts a servant's nature, expressed as race-based enslavement that he compares to the mindset of Arab regimes; leading people to the fire; and the result, a curse that outlives him and ugliness on the Day of Judgement. He develops true imamate as leading from the front, as the Prophet did by putting his own family first in battle, and warns that everyone is an imam over someone, so speak only with knowledge. Verse 43 pairs guidance with mercy: guidance that does not produce mercy is not guidance. Verse 44, 'you were not there', reveals the surah's axis: do not judge stories you did not witness.

outline.heading: Recap: Pharaoh's emotional appeal and the tower
outline.gist: Pharaoh had no real argument, so he posed as caring for his people and as seriously investigating Musa's claim.

outline.heading: Everyone should learn the logical fallacies
outline.gist: Most attacks on religion and on reason come through fallacies; anyone reaching adulthood should know them.

outline.heading: The loaded question: a stone Allah cannot move
outline.gist: To create already means having power over the created, so the question contradicts itself, like asking the smell of green.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's straw man
outline.gist: He recast Musa's watertight claim into a weak one, that Musa's Lord sits where a tower could reach, and refuted that; his media then drowned out Musa's correction.

outline.heading: Arguing against what you assume someone's words imply
outline.gist: Much sectarian dispute and most marital conflict comes from attacking a conclusion the other never stated; first ask whether the words really entail it.

outline.heading: Prolonging a problem until people lose interest
outline.gist: Attention lasts about six weeks; the ummah held out over Gaza for twelve before fading, as with Iraq, Syria, Libya and the Rohingya. Solve problems within a month.

outline.heading: Truth speaks for itself and needs no loud claims
outline.gist: Musa only asked to let Allah and evidence judge; Muslims must never resort to fallacies and should follow better evidence wherever it is.

outline.heading: Straw man plus delay; the story now gives way to commentary
outline.gist: The tower bought years while Bani Israil stayed enslaved; the coming verses comment on Pharaoh's fate rather than retell events.

outline.heading: Recitation: arrogance, drowning and the lasting curse
outline.gist: He recites the passage and notes holding the ghunnah on a doubled meem when stopping.

outline.heading: Arrogance contradicts what a servant is
outline.gist: A servant was made to serve; only the Lord is rightly al-Mutakabbir, so arrogance puts a weak creature in a station not his own. Pharaoh needed soldiers to make him a pharaoh.

outline.heading: Race-based slavery: a deeper evil
outline.gist: Arab slavery came from debt or war, not birth; Pharaoh enslaved a whole race and convinced both sides it was the natural order.

outline.heading: The same mindset under Arab regimes
outline.gist: People across the Arab world accepted that ruling families are born above them and that the disappeared must not be asked about; this is consent to servitude.

outline.heading: The return to Allah, and seeking justice now
outline.gist: The Hour exists to set such wrongs right, but waiting for Judgement Day while accepting tyranny is cowardice; Musa demanded rights alongside tawhid.

outline.heading: The sea parts and Pharaoh is cast in
outline.gist: Musa did not know what to do with the sea ahead and the army behind until told to strike; nabadha means discarding with contempt, as in nabidh left to spoil.

outline.heading: The true meaning of imam: the one who goes first
outline.gist: An imam walks ahead of people through what they will face, as Ibrahim did; leadership from a dark room is not imamate.

outline.heading: The Prophet put his own family first
outline.gist: At Badr he sent Ali, Hamzah and Ubaydah ibn al-Harith to the duel and Ali at the Trench; he never asked others to do what he did not.

outline.heading: Leading from the front, even into the fire
outline.gist: The companions were shamed into effort by his sacrifice and sheltered behind him in battle; Pharaoh likewise walks ahead of his people into the fire.

outline.heading: An imam shares what his people endure
outline.gist: Unlike a king, the Prophet was hungriest, most afraid and most harmed, living on what Bilal hid under his arm during the boycott.

outline.heading: You are an imam whether you like it or not
outline.gist: Pulpits and leading prayer are a burden to be questioned about; every person leads a household, a friend, or at least himself, toward paradise or the fire.

outline.heading: Calling others to the fire is a second, heavier crime
outline.gist: Misguiding others differs from misguiding yourself; the reward for guiding one person outweighs the world, and the burden of misleading is as great.

outline.heading: Speak about the deen only with knowledge
outline.gist: Some callers would serve Islam best by silence; youth are often lost through cultural claims at home passed off as religion.

outline.heading: A curse that outlives his kingdom
outline.gist: Knowledge comes through generations back to the Prophet, not from a video; Pharaoh's legacy is a curse on every tongue for thousands of years after a reign of decades.

outline.heading: Among the disfigured on the Day of Judgement
outline.gist: Maqbuhin: placed where onlookers see only ugliness; this is the end of arrogance, tyranny and misleading others.

outline.heading: Appearances deceive: why Musa was told to speak gently
outline.gist: Pharaoh looked mighty but was cursed and doomed, so gentleness was mercy toward a loser; the sheikh describes his own earlier unease with these verses.

3ntbKqNg7m0.title: Activism, Our Path Forward: The Pursuit of Guidance for All
3ntbKqNg7m0.one_line: The objective of Muslim activism is guidance for ourselves and all people; liberation and unity follow on the way, as the Prophet's life shows.
3ntbKqNg7m0.summary: Nine months into the massacre in the Holy Land, he insists Muslims must learn from it. The protests revealed that Muslims in the West have numbers, youth and wealth; what is missing is activism, devoting oneself to a cause beyond oneself. But the objective is not liberation; liberation, unity and wellbeing are consequences. The objective is guidance for ourselves and others. The youths of the cave retreated to plan because their people were misguided, and guidance means honesty, trustworthiness, incorruptibility and equality, not only prayer. Muslims ask for it at least seventeen times a day, and true victory is people entering the religion in crowds. Work, family and wealth should all point toward that goal; a routine life of work, bills and leisure is not what the Prophet lived, and no one is remembered for it. Guidance is ongoing, so converts and children need lasting support, and it includes standing for truth against oppression. In the second khutbah he shows the Prophet's single-minded dedication: he prayed the funeral of Abdullah ibn Ubayy, his worst enemy, swallowing his own feelings for one more soul. He closes with Thumamah ibn Uthal, who accepted Islam after three days tied in the masjid watching the companions, and asks what a visitor would see in ours.

outline.heading: Opening
Every hardship must leave a lesson
outline.gist: Nine months into the massacre that Muslims failed to stop, he insists that going through an atrocity without learning how to prevent it, or soften its consequences next time, is unacceptable to Allah.

outline.heading: Why this atrocity is different
outline.gist: He never expected such brutality in his lifetime. Conflicts in Syria, Lebanon, Sudan or Bangladesh are Muslims failing each other; this is an attack from outside, which changes how it lands.

outline.heading: What the protests revealed
outline.gist: The land carries religious weight, and the encampments and marches across Europe and North America showed how many Muslims live in the West, with youth and wealth.

outline.heading: What we lack is activism
outline.gist: Not numbers but activism; even leadership is impossible without an activist people. Activism is dedicating yourself to a cause beyond you and arranging everything else to serve it.

outline.heading: Liberation is a consequence, guidance is the objective
outline.gist: Last week was why you do it; today is what for. Liberation, unity and the wellbeing of Muslims follow on the way, but the objective is guidance for yourself and others, and losing sight of it makes everything crumble.

outline.heading: The cave: a space to reflect and plan
outline.gist: The cave is symbolic: every movement needs a mental and communal space to assess and plan. The youths knew their objective, doubted it was achievable as a handful of teenagers, and saw their people walking a crooked path without proof.

outline.heading: Guidance is more than prayer
outline.gist: Their people lied about Allah (18:15). Guidance means honesty, trustworthiness, incorruptibility, refusing oppression and treating everyone as equals, and if Islam was not taught to you with these first, you were mistaught.

outline.heading: Asked for seventeen times a day
outline.gist: Anyone listening to a Muslim would think him obsessed with guidance: he asks for the straight path at least seventeen times a day (1:6).

outline.heading: Victory is people entering the faith
outline.gist: When Allah's help comes, the victory is people entering His religion in crowds (110:1-2), not others submitting to our strength; once people hold to truth, injustice fades on its own.

outline.heading: Only Allah guides, and He gives clarity
outline.gist: The line he recites in every khutbah opening comes from this story: whom Allah guides is guided (18:17). The youths asked for right guidance (18:10); being an activist means spreading that guidance in gratitude for it.

outline.heading: Family and work in service of guidance
outline.gist: The point of a family is to raise people who carry guidance forward; you work to provide for them and keep time free to push guidance further.

outline.heading: No one remembers you for paying your bills
outline.gist: A life of work, food, sleep and holidays is not how the Prophet or his followers lived. No one knows the companions' wives or homes; they are remembered for their dedication, without which this masjid would not exist.

outline.heading: Why are you doing it?
outline.gist: Marriage, children and work done for culture or to please parents are not worth it. Every arrow, wealth, family, knowledge and work, must point to the one goal of guidance.

outline.heading: Zoom out: guidance for all mankind
outline.gist: Guidance means recognizing truth and falsehood and refusing oppression. Making the cause one place loses the picture; the cause is guidance for all of Adam's children, and unity and liberation come on the way.

outline.heading: Guiding one person; guidance is ongoing
outline.gist: Allah guiding one person through you is better than the world, but guidance is not a single shahada; you have asked for it in every prayer for decades.

outline.heading: Guide by living rightly, then stay with them
outline.gist: People follow someone they see living correctly. Bringing a convert to the shahada and leaving him cut off from family, work and language achieves nothing; the same applies to our children.

outline.heading: Advocacy and activism are means
outline.gist: Advocacy and activism are methods toward the objective of guidance, not the objective itself.

outline.heading: Interlude
A dedication nothing could cloud
outline.gist: The Prophet wanted guidance for others on a level he admits he cannot emulate. Activism is when nothing clouds your view of the objective; he introduces the Bukhari account of Abdullah ibn Ubayy.

outline.heading: Ibn Ubayy, the Prophet's worst enemy
outline.gist: Head of the hypocrites in Madinah, he slandered the Prophet's wife, urged people to withhold their spending, pulled a third of the army out before battle and made over fifteen attempts to end Islam.

outline.heading: Insulted on the way to a dying woman
outline.gist: Riding past Ibn Ubayy's door, the Prophet was told his animal stank up the neighbourhood. He ignored it and went to stand at the bedside of a dying elderly woman whom no one else would visit.

outline.heading: The boast of the superior and the dog
outline.gist: Ibn Ubayy said the honourable would expel the lowly from Madinah (63:8) and compared the Muslims to a dog that eats its owner. His son Abdullah, by contrast, was a good man.

outline.heading: The shirt and the seventy times
outline.gist: The son asked for the Prophet's shirt to shroud his father. The Prophet gave it and went to pray, while Umar pulled him back reminding him of each insult and of the verse about seventy requests for forgiveness (9:80).

outline.heading: The funeral prayer before the verse came
outline.gist: The Prophet read 9:80 as a choice, placed Ibn Ubayy in his own shirt and prayed over him; only then was 9:84 revealed. Allah let it happen first so we would watch his mindset.

outline.heading: Not even kin, and never any goodness
outline.gist: He admits there are people he would celebrate the death of. Abu Jahl and Abu Lahab were at least relatives; Ibn Ubayy had no tie to the Prophet and showed him nothing but hatred and betrayal.

outline.heading: One more soul to Jannah
outline.gist: He reads the funeral not sentimentally but as activism: if the price of someone reaching Paradise is swallowing your ego and setting aside the pain, the Prophet paid it.

outline.heading: Guidance in every domain
outline.gist: Guidance is recognizing truth, falsehood and the causes to stand for; prayer with acceptance of oppression is missing something. He asks to be guided with Allah, the Prophet, community, family, neighbours and all humanity.

outline.heading: Thumamah, a king of the rival tribe
outline.gist: The Adnani Arabs split into Mudar, the Prophet's branch, and Rabi'ah, who long fought each other. Thumamah ibn Uthal was a king of Rabi'ah.

outline.heading: Three days tied in the masjid
outline.gist: Thumamah funded two of the nine attempts on the Prophet's life, was captured and tied to a pillar of the masjid. Each day the Prophet asked how he was and walked away from his offers; on the third day he freed him, and Thumamah bathed and returned to accept Islam after watching the companions' devotion and compassion.

outline.heading: What would a visitor see in our masjid?
outline.gist: The Prophet was not interested in ransom or revenge but in whether Thumamah had found Allah. If someone watched our masjid for three days, what would they conclude?

outline.heading: The missing piece in the Muslim heart
outline.gist: If that dedication returns to the collective Muslim heart, things change faster than imagined, as Muslim history shows. He hopes the generation that watched these nine months will carry it.

outline.heading: Outro

35:18.en: And no burdened soul can bear another's burden, and if one heavy laden crieth for (help with) his load, naught of it will be lifted even though he (unto whom he crieth) be of kin. Thou warnest only those who fear their Lord in secret, and have established worship. He who groweth (in goodness), groweth only for himself, (he cannot by his merit redeem others). Unto Allah is the journeying

29:6.ar: وَمَن جَٰهَدَ فَإِنَّمَا يُجَٰهِدُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عَنِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
29:6.en: And whosoever striveth, striveth only for himself, for lo! Allah is altogether Independent of (His) creatures

41:46.ar: مَّنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَلِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَنۡ أَسَآءَ فَعَلَيۡهَاۗ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِظَلَّٰمࣲ لِّلۡعَبِيدِ
41:46.en: Whoso doeth right it is for his soul, and whoso doeth wrong it is against it. And thy Lord is not at all a tyrant to His slaves

31:12.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا لُقۡمَٰنَ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ أَنِ ٱشۡكُرۡ لِلَّهِۚ وَمَن يَشۡكُرۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدࣱ‏
31:12.en: And verily We gave Luqman wisdom, saying: Give thanks unto Allah; and whosoever giveth thanks, he giveth thanks for (the good of) his soul. And whosoever refuseth - Lo! Allah is Absolute, Owner of Praise

2:272.ar: ۞لَّيۡسَ عَلَيۡكَ هُدَىٰهُمۡ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۗ وَمَا تُنفِقُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ فَلِأَنفُسِكُمۡۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُونَ إِلَّا ٱبۡتِغَآءَ وَجۡهِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ يُوَفَّ إِلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تُظۡلَمُونَ
2:272.en: The guiding of them is not thy duty (O Muhammad), but Allah guideth whom He will. And whatsoever good thing ye spend, it is for yourselves, when ye spend not save in search of Allah's Countenance; and whatsoever good thing ye spend, it will be repaid to you in full, and ye will not be wronged

17:7.ar: إِنۡ أَحۡسَنتُمۡ أَحۡسَنتُمۡ لِأَنفُسِكُمۡۖ وَإِنۡ أَسَأۡتُمۡ فَلَهَاۚ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعۡدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ لِيَسُـُٔواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ وَلِيَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَلِيُتَبِّرُواْ مَا عَلَوۡاْ تَتۡبِيرًا
17:7.en: (Saying): If ye do good, ye do good for your own souls, and if ye do evil, it is for them (in like manner). So, when the time for the second (of the judgments) came (We roused against you others of Our slaves) to ravage you, and to enter the Temple even as they entered it the first time, and to lay waste all that they conquered with an utter wasting

65:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وَأَحۡصُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّكُمۡۖ لَا تُخۡرِجُوهُنَّ مِنۢ بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلَا يَخۡرُجۡنَ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةࣲ مُّبَيِّنَةࣲۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ ظَلَمَ نَفۡسَهُۥۚ لَا تَدۡرِي لَعَلَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحۡدِثُ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ أَمۡرࣰ ا
65:1.en: O Prophet! When ye (men) put away women, put them away for their (legal) period and reckon the period, and keep your duty to Allah, your Lord. Expel them not from their houses nor let them go forth unless they commit open immorality. Such are the limits (imposed by) Allah; and whoso transgresseth Allah's limits, he verily wrongeth his soul. Thou knowest not: it may be that Allah will afterward bring some new thing to pass

3:69.ar: وَدَّت طَّآئِفَةࣱ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَوۡ يُضِلُّونَكُمۡ وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَمَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
3:69.en: A party of the People of the Scripture long to make you go astray; and they make none to go astray except themselves, but they perceive not

26:12.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
26:12.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! I fear that they will deny me

26:13.ar: وَيَضِيقُ صَدۡرِي وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِي فَأَرۡسِلۡ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
26:13.en: And I shall be embarrassed, and my tongue will not speak plainly, therefor send for Aaron (to help me)

Byah-ySZ2OI.speaker: adnan
Byah-ySZ2OI.speaker_note: Continues his own 'Activism - Our Path Forward' series in first person; one voice throughout, typical khutbah structure.
Byah-ySZ2OI.title: Activism - Our Path Forward: Answering the Why
Byah-ySZ2OI.one_line: Why we obey Allah and serve others at all: the Quran says every good deed benefits you, so aim your selfishness at Jannah.
Byah-ySZ2OI.summary: Opening the new Hijri year in the middle of his activism series, the sheikh pauses to ask the foundational question: why do we obey Allah, why serve anyone, why sit in a khutbah at all? Fear of punishment cannot carry a person for life, so the real answer must be internalized. He builds it from a string of Quranic phrases that all end the same way: whoever gains insight, guidance, purification, strives, does good, is grateful or gives, does so for himself, and whoever transgresses only wrongs himself. The conclusion is blunt: nobody owes you for anything you do; you do it to save yourself. He then flips the Western focus on the individual rather than rejecting it: a truly selfish person would want Jannah above everything, and the only road there is a life of service, so be selfless in this world in order to be selfish in the next. He illustrates this with the father of Jabir choosing Uhud over his son, and in the second khutbah with the Prophet's hereafter-centred life: unprovokable, dying with a pawned shield, yet asking us to pray for his highest rank. He closes with the Muharram memories of the Hijrah, Musa before Pharaoh and Husayn, asking people to revise their intention and give fully, for their own sake.

outline.heading: Opening
The new year: a moment to review yourself
outline.gist: He is not one for retelling the annual stories, but the start of the Hijri year, in its sacred month, is a chance to review the past year, plan what to do differently, and ask who we are, why we live as we do and where we are going.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf 18:29: you are not doing this for anyone else
outline.gist: The verse right after the story of the people of the cave: the truth is from your Lord, so let whoever wills believe and whoever wills disbelieve. Belief strengthens nothing for Allah; you are not doing it for someone else's benefit.

outline.heading: Why do any of this? Fear is short-lived
outline.gist: Why care about others, obey Allah, stand at the minbar or sit in a khutbah every Friday? 'Because Allah commanded' and 'because of the punishment' are not enough: fear fades and cannot motivate a lifetime.

outline.heading: Al-An'am 6:104: insight is for yourself
outline.gist: The answer must be internalized below the conscious level. The Quran says it directly fifteen or twenty times: insight has come from your Lord, and whoever sees does so for his own benefit.

outline.heading: You serve others for your own sake
outline.gist: Do not fool yourself that you serve people for their sake; Allah made serving others the only way to make it, so you serve them to help yourself. Stop doing it for others and do it because Allah commanded it and it benefits you.

outline.heading: Whoever is guided is guided for himself
outline.gist: Four times the Quran says that whoever accepts guidance does so for his own benefit, in this life and the next.

outline.heading: Purity, striving, good deeds and gratitude are for yourself
outline.gist: Whoever purifies himself does it for himself; whoever strives strives for himself, and Allah needs no one; whoever does good does it for himself; and Luqman was told that whoever is grateful is grateful for himself.

outline.heading: Giving and excellence are for yourself
outline.gist: When you take money out of your pocket and give, you give to yourself; when you show excellence, it is for you. No one owes you anything for what you do.

outline.heading: No one owes you: Allah rewards what never benefited Him
outline.gist: Even selfless acts for Allah earn you no debt: your deeds give Him nothing, yet He rewards them many times over. Whoever lives for Allah as an activist does it to save himself.

outline.heading: The reverse: whoever transgresses wrongs himself
outline.gist: Spreading knowledge, building community and caring for the needy are all for yourself; anyone who told you otherwise lied. The same language runs the other way: they only misguide and oppress themselves, and whoever oversteps Allah's limits wrongs himself.

outline.heading: Strengthen the focus on the individual
outline.gist: This is one of the clearest themes in the whole Quran. The West focuses on the individual and his happiness; rather than fight that, he says strengthen it, because true self-interest leads somewhere.

outline.heading: Jannah, the most selfish goal, reached by service
outline.gist: Nothing beats making it to Jannah for selfishness, and this world is too short to compete. Allah's guidance says the only road there is living in service of others: be selfless in this world to be selfish in the next.

outline.heading: Selfishness is instinct: aim it at the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: We are selfish by nature and cannot change it; people with no wants at all are like the shell-shocked, not truly alive. The question is whether you aim your selfishness at the Day of Judgment, as the Prophet did when he offered his relatives his wealth but said only they could save themselves from the Fire.

outline.heading: Jabir's father at Uhud: anything but Jannah
outline.gist: An elderly father of many daughters and his son Jabir both prepared for battle, though one had to stay with the family. They drew lots and the father won, telling his tearful son that he would yield anything to him except Jannah. That was how they understood life: save yourself first.

outline.heading: Everyone seeks a reward: make yours salvation
outline.gist: No one is selfless without some reward, whether reputation, moral superiority or silencing an annoying conscience. At the start of the year, revise your intention so the reward you seek is Allah saving you on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Interlude
He could not be provoked
outline.gist: The Prophet's ambition was the Hereafter, so nothing could provoke him. When a man insulted him until the companions wanted to strike him, he held them back and said they should have told the man to ask nicely and reminded him to repay well.

outline.heading: He died with his shield in pawn
outline.gist: The man testified that he was the Messenger of Allah, saying his scripture foretold that mistreatment only made him more patient. At sixty-three the Prophet died with his war shield pawned for a loan and left nothing to inherit, because his interest in the world was zero.

outline.heading: His one request: al-wasilah
outline.gist: He asked many things of us for our own sake and one for himself: pray that Allah gives him al-wasilah, a rank granted to only one person. He did not say someone else could have the higher status.

outline.heading: Ask for the highest point of Jannah
outline.gist: Give others the front seat in this world, but do not be selfless about the Hereafter. When you ask Allah, ask for the highest point, not just to be let in at the door; save humility for when your deeds are no longer recorded.

outline.heading: The Hijrah: losing home and country for the cause
outline.gist: While deeds are still recorded, gain insight, give and strive for yourself. The new year recalls the Hijrah, and many scholars hold fasting in this month sunnah. The Prophet left his home for good and found it torn down when he returned; homes are still being torn down and others moved in, and giving everything for the cause is the ultimate activism.

outline.heading: Musa before Pharaoh: going despite fear
outline.gist: Many here have already relocated for their faith; continue the path. On Ashura Allah saved Musa after one of history's most courageous acts: facing a dictator who enslaved a people and called himself god. Musa admitted his fear and asked for Harun, then went anyway.

outline.heading: Husayn refused oppression
outline.gist: Husayn saw oppression that did not represent Islam or his grandfather's legacy, refused to accept it and spoke out. These days hold the memory of people who gave everything they had.

outline.heading: Do it for yourself, and go the full extent
outline.gist: Do not do it for your people or nation but to save yourself, and Allah will put a love, closeness and clarity in your heart that you will carry for life. You came to have your Jumuah accepted; prioritize saving yourself, and go the full extent rather than stopping halfway.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: The whole first khutbah argues that the correct intention behind worship, service and activism is self-interest rightly aimed: you do it to save yourself, and the new year is the time to revise that intention.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: He keeps asking 'why' past the usual answers (because Allah commanded, because of punishment) until he reaches a motive that can last a lifetime.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: A thematic reading across many verses showing how often the Quran says a deed is 'for yourself'; he calls it one of the clearest themes in the whole book.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Jannah is presented as the ultimate selfish desire; the whole dunya is too short to compete with it, so every choice should be weighed against the Day of Judgment.

themes.label: Muslim identity and life in the West / Canada
themes.note: The Western emphasis on the individual is not the enemy; properly understood, individual self-interest leads straight to serving others for Jannah.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Abdullah ibn Amr and his son Jabir drawing lots over who goes to Uhud shows how the companions saw saving themselves as the priority.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: His forbearance under provocation, his poverty at death, and his single request for al-wasilah show a life whose ambition was entirely in the Hereafter.

themes.label: Activism, civic engagement and the path forward
themes.note: The Hijrah, Musa confronting Pharaoh and Husayn's stand are presented as the ultimate activism: giving everything for the cause, while remembering you do it for your own salvation.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: The Prophet left Makkah never to live there again and found his home torn down when he returned; he compares this to people whose homes are demolished today.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Musa admitted fear before Pharaoh and asked for Harun, yet went; Ashura commemorates that courage.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Brief but pointed: homes are still being torn down and others moved in, 'last week or last century makes no difference'.

stories.who: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram and his son Jabir before Uhud
stories.point: Father and son both insisted on going; they drew lots and the father won, telling his son he would yield anything except Jannah. The companions understood that saving yourself comes first.

stories.who: Zayd ibn Sa'nah provoking the Prophet
stories.point: The Prophet could not be provoked; his patience under abuse was itself the sign that convinced the man to accept Islam.

stories.who: The Prophet's Hijrah and demolished home
stories.point: He left country and home for Islam, never to live there again, and found his house torn down on return; this is the ultimate activism, and it mirrors what happens to displaced people today.

He saw oppression that did not represent his grandfather's legacy and refused to accept it, speaking out at the cost of everything.

takeaways: Use the start of the Hijri year to review the past year and revise why you do what you do.
Fix in your mind that every act of worship, service and giving benefits you first; expect nothing from people in return.
Direct your natural self-interest at the Day of Judgment: ask Allah for the highest rank in Jannah and do not settle for less.
Serve others, build the community and spread knowledge as the only road to saving yourself, not as a favour to anyone.
Remember the Hijrah, Musa and Husayn this month and be willing to give what you have for the cause, fully and not half-heartedly.

64:14.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ مِنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَٰدِكُمۡ عَدُوࣰّ ا لَّكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُمۡۚ وَإِن تَعۡفُواْ وَتَصۡفَحُواْ وَتَغۡفِرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
64:14.en: O ye who believe! Lo! among your wives and your children there are enemies for you, therefor beware of them. And if ye efface and overlook and forgive, then lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

64:15.ar: إِنَّمَآ أَمۡوَٰلُكُمۡ وَأَوۡلَٰدُكُمۡ فِتۡنَةࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُۥٓ أَجۡرٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
64:15.en: Your wealth and your children are only a temptation, whereas Allah! with Him is an immense reward

64:16.ar: فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ وَٱسۡمَعُواْ وَأَطِيعُواْ وَأَنفِقُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا لِّأَنفُسِكُمۡۗ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
64:16.en: So keep your duty to Allah as best ye can, and listen, and obey, and spend; that is better for your souls. And whoso is saved from his own greed, such are the successful

64:17.ar: إِن تُقۡرِضُواْ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنࣰ ا يُضَٰعِفۡهُ لَكُمۡ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ
64:17.en: If ye lend unto Allah a goodly loan, He will double it for you and will forgive you, for Allah is Responsive, Clement

64:18.en: Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, the Mighty, the Wise

64:9.ar: يَوۡمَ يَجۡمَعُكُمۡ لِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡجَمۡعِۖ ذَٰلِكَ يَوۡمُ ٱلتَّغَابُنِۗ وَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ وَيَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحࣰ ا يُكَفِّرۡ عَنۡهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِۦ وَيُدۡخِلۡهُ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
64:9.en: The day when He shall gather you unto the Day of Assembling, that will be a day of mutual disillusion. And whoso believeth in Allah and doeth right, He will remit from him his evil deeds and will bring him unto Gardens underneath which rivers flow, therein to abide for ever. That is the supreme triumph

2:284.ar: لِّلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ وَإِن تُبۡدُواْ مَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوۡ تُخۡفُوهُ يُحَاسِبۡكُم بِهِ ٱللَّهُۖ فَيَغۡفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
2:284.en: Unto Allah (belongeth) whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth; and whether ye make known what is in your minds or hide it, Allah will bring you to account for it. He will forgive whom He will and He will punish whom He will. Allah is Able to do all things

33:28.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيۡنَ أُمَتِّعۡكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحۡكُنَّ سَرَاحࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
33:28.en: O Prophet! Say unto thy wives: If ye desire the world's life and its adornment, come! I will content you and will release you with a fair release

33:29.ar: وَإِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلۡمُحۡسِنَٰتِ مِنكُنَّ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
33:29.en: But if ye desire Allah and His messenger and the abode of the Hereafter, then lo! Allah hath prepared for the good among you an immense reward

59:9.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ يُحِبُّونَ مَنۡ هَاجَرَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ حَاجَةࣰ مِّمَّآ أُوتُواْ وَيُؤۡثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَلَوۡ كَانَ بِهِمۡ خَصَاصَةࣱۚ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
59:9.en: Those who entered the city and the faith before them love those who flee unto them for refuge, and find in their breasts no need for that which hath been given them, but prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot. And whoso is saved from his own avarice - such are they who are successful

17:79.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَتَهَجَّدۡ بِهِۦ نَافِلَةࣰ لَّكَ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَبۡعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامࣰ ا مَّحۡمُودࣰ ا
17:79.en: And some part of the night awake for it, a largess for thee. It may be that thy Lord will raise thee to a praised estate

2:276.ar: يَمۡحَقُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرِّبَوٰاْ وَيُرۡبِي ٱلصَّدَقَٰتِۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ أَثِيمٍ
2:276.en: Allah hath blighted usury and made almsgiving fruitful. Allah loveth not the impious and guilty

50Z7kqOR_JI.speaker_note: his own weekly tafseer course, continuing the Al-Taghabun series
50Z7kqOR_JI.title: Surat Al-Taghabun, Part 4 (Verses 14-18)
50Z7kqOR_JI.one_line: Al-Taghabun 14-18: family who act as enemies, wealth and children as trials, taqwa to one's capacity, selflessness, and lending Allah a good loan.
50Z7kqOR_JI.summary: Closing the surah, he returns to its theme: amid technical Medinan rulings, it reminds believers why they act. Verse 14 calls some spouses and children enemies, a word only Allah could use, and he calls its command the hardest in the Quran: do not cut them off, but guard your intention and pardon, overlook and conceal. This is only possible if you served them for Allah, since verse 15 says wealth and children are trials and you deal with Allah through them. The same principle governs applying Islamic law: Umar suspended the hand-cutting penalty in a famine because rulings must serve their purpose, while coercion in Muslim countries has bred backlash. He counsels parents in the West not to disown children who stray. Verse 16 eased the companions: taqwa is awareness that asks whether something displeases Allah, done to one's own capacity, which no one else can set. He contrasts this with the Prophet's unmatched selflessness, leaving nothing at his death. Hear and accept Islam whole without modifying it, give from whatever you have, and beware selfishness, redirecting it toward the Hereafter. Verse 17 frames charity as a loan Allah repays many times over, and generosity covers faults. The closing names remind you why you do all this.

outline.heading: Opening
The second group of comprehensive surahs and its Medinan juz
outline.gist: Juz 28 is fully Medinan, revealed late in the Prophet's life, and focuses on organizing the Muslim community.

outline.heading: Spiritual verses inside technical surahs
outline.gist: Whenever the Quran turns legal, it inserts reminders of why you follow the rulings: to please Allah, not out of habit.

outline.heading: Recap: the Day of mutual deceit
outline.gist: On the Day of Taghabun every claimed motive disappears and only the real reasons remain.

outline.heading: Interlude
"Enemies to you": a word only Allah could use
outline.gist: Some of those you serve most may actively work against you, not merely fail to support you.

outline.heading: Examples from the Sunnah
outline.gist: People whose families delayed their Islam so they missed companionship, and a man whose wife and children kept him from expeditions.

outline.heading: Beware: protect your intention in daily routines
outline.gist: The command is to guard why you serve them, or you lose both the goal and the intention.

outline.heading: The hardest command: keep serving them for Allah
outline.gist: A father's instinct is to walk away, but the verse says beware, not remove them; they are recipients of service done for Allah.

outline.heading: Self-interest masked as sincerity
outline.gist: If you were serving for Allah, their hostility would not make you hostile; difficulty here exposes a hidden agenda.

outline.heading: Pardon, overlook, conceal
outline.gist: The three words address the act, the person and exposure; he excludes abusive situations, which need professional help.

outline.heading: Wealth and children are only a trial
outline.gist: Everything you are given is a test from Allah, so you deal with Allah through your family whether they are allies or enemies.

outline.heading: Rulings can be applied against their own purpose
outline.gist: Applying fiqh without asking whom you are pleasing can defeat the ruling's objective.

outline.heading: Umar suspends the theft penalty in famine
outline.gist: Umar stopped courts from cutting hands during starvation, understanding that each ruling needs the right environment to serve its aim.

outline.heading: Coercion backfires
outline.gist: Forcing prayer, dress or business closures looks orderly but breeds hatred that later explodes, as seen in parts of the Gulf.

outline.heading: When children in the West make heartbreaking choices
outline.gist: Parents ask whether to cut children off; the Quran says beware and forgive, not sever, and a child who strays is not even an enemy.

outline.heading: You are no better than the prophets
outline.gist: Prophets too had spouses and children who chose otherwise; this is no licence for the young to go rogue.

outline.heading: A great reward, and life is short
outline.gist: The reward outweighs the trial; ask anyone in their eighties how quickly life passed, and settle your intentions early.

outline.heading: Intentions cannot be overemphasized
outline.gist: The motive matters, not just the result; the ends do not justify the means.

outline.heading: Interlude
A verse that relieved the companions
outline.gist: After the fear caused by being accountable for what is in the self, "as much as you are able" brought ease.

outline.heading: Taqwa: asking "will this displease Allah?"
outline.gist: Taqwa is preventive awareness before every decision; asking what displeases Allah leaves the large permissible space open, while asking what pleases Him is the harder path of the elite.

outline.heading: The Prophet's unmatched standard
outline.gist: He gave without return, kept no long-term plan, spent on others and died owning nothing, his shield pawned for a loan made to help someone.

outline.heading: No leisure in his life: joy in closeness to Allah
outline.gist: People need some leisure, but he found his rest in prayer, Quran and service, a transformation that takes a lifetime.

outline.heading: "As much as you can": only you know your capacity
outline.gist: The Prophet qualified the pledge by ability; asking others to set your capacity is unfair, since they give either their own level or an ideal they do not meet.

outline.heading: The choice given to the Prophet's wives
outline.gist: They were offered release with wealth or life on his terms with no plan of improvement, and all chose him; his clarity of intention made such a life possible.

outline.heading: Hear and obey: accept Islam as it is
outline.gist: You may fall short, but do not modify Islam to suit yourself or the values of the country you live in.

outline.heading: Give from whatever you have
outline.gist: Spending is not only money but time, energy, knowledge and expertise.

outline.heading: Protected from the selfishness of the soul
outline.gist: Shuhh is wanting personal gain from religion or work; a physician steering patients to a drug for kickbacks is corruption.

outline.heading: Serving Allah as delayed selfishness
outline.gist: Humans cannot stop being selfish; redirect it toward reward and closeness to Allah instead of worldly gain.

outline.heading: The Prophet's only selfish request
outline.gist: He asked nothing for himself except that we pray for him to be granted the praised station on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: The recipe: awareness, acceptance, giving
outline.gist: Taqwa to your ability, full acceptance, generous giving and freedom from selfishness.

outline.heading: Interlude
A goodly loan to Allah, repaid with increase
outline.gist: Allah calls charity a loan He repays many times over, like a foal raised into a steed, with forgiveness as a bonus.

outline.heading: Generosity covers every flaw
outline.gist: Old Arab wisdom: be generous to cover your faults; a husband who falls short should at least not be stingy. Allah is Shakur and Halim.

outline.heading: Closing names: the reason for everything
outline.gist: The surah ends with five names of Allah as it began with His majesty, reminding you that you do all this because of who He is.

28:44.ar: وَمَا كُنتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلۡغَرۡبِيِّ إِذۡ قَضَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلۡأَمۡرَ وَمَا كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
28:44.en: And thou (Muhammad) wast not on the western side (of the Mount) when We expounded unto Moses the commandment, and thou wast not among those present

28:45.ar: وَلَٰكِنَّآ أَنشَأۡنَا قُرُونࣰ ا فَتَطَاوَلَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡعُمُرُۚ وَمَا كُنتَ ثَاوِيࣰ ا فِيٓ أَهۡلِ مَدۡيَنَ تَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا كُنَّا مُرۡسِلِينَ
28:45.en: But We brought forth generations, and their lives dragged on for them. And thou wast not a dweller in Midian, reciting unto them Our revelations, but We kept sending (messengers to men)

28:46.ar: وَمَا كُنتَ بِجَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ إِذۡ نَادَيۡنَا وَلَٰكِن رَّحۡمَةࣰ مِّن رَّبِّكَ لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أَتَىٰهُم مِّن نَّذِيرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
28:46.en: And thou was not beside the Mount when We did call; but (the knowledge of it is) a mercy from thy Lord that thou mayst warn a folk unto whom no warner came before thee, that haply they may give heed

28:47.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن تُصِيبَهُم مُّصِيبَةُۢ بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ فَيَقُولُواْ رَبَّنَا لَوۡلَآ أَرۡسَلۡتَ إِلَيۡنَا رَسُولࣰ ا فَنَتَّبِعَ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
28:47.en: Otherwise, if disaster should afflict them because of that which their own hands have sent before (them), they might say: Our Lord! Why sentest Thou no messenger unto us, that we might have followed Thy revelations and been of the believers

28:48.ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِنۡ عِندِنَا قَالُواْ لَوۡلَآ أُوتِيَ مِثۡلَ مَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰٓۚ أَوَلَمۡ يَكۡفُرُواْ بِمَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ مِن قَبۡلُۖ قَالُواْ سِحۡرَانِ تَظَٰهَرَا وَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِكُلࣲّ كَٰفِرُونَ
28:48.en: But when there came unto them the Truth from Our presence, they said: Why is he not given the like of what was given unto Moses? Did they not disbelieve in that which was given unto Moses of old? They say: Two magics that support each other; and they say: Lo! in both we are disbelievers

28:49.ar: قُلۡ فَأۡتُواْ بِكِتَٰبࣲ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ أَهۡدَىٰ مِنۡهُمَآ أَتَّبِعۡهُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
28:49.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Then bring a scripture from the presence of Allah that giveth clearer guidance than these two (that) I may follow it, if ye are truthful

28:50.ar: فَإِن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لَكَ فَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّمَا يَتَّبِعُونَ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡۚ وَمَنۡ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ بِغَيۡرِ هُدࣰ ى مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
28:50.en: And if they answer thee not, then know that what they follow is their lusts. And who goeth farther astray than he who followeth his lust without guidance from Allah. Lo! Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

28:30.ar: فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِيَ مِن شَٰطِيِٕ ٱلۡوَادِ ٱلۡأَيۡمَنِ فِي ٱلۡبُقۡعَةِ ٱلۡمُبَٰرَكَةِ مِنَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ أَن يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّيٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
28:30.en: And when he reached it, he was called from the right side of the valley in the blessed field, from the tree: O Moses! Lo! I, even I, am Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

28:31.ar: وَأَنۡ أَلۡقِ عَصَاكَۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهۡتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَآنࣱّ وَلَّىٰ مُدۡبِرࣰ ا وَلَمۡ يُعَقِّبۡۚ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَقۡبِلۡ وَلَا تَخَفۡۖ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓمِنِينَ
28:31.en: Throw down thy staff. And when he saw it writhing as it had been a demon, he turned to flee headlong, (and it was said unto him): O Moses! Draw nigh and fear not. Lo! thou art of those who are secure

85:10.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَتَنُواْ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَتُوبُواْ فَلَهُمۡ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابُ ٱلۡحَرِيقِ
85:10.en: Lo! they who persecute believing men and believing women and repent not, theirs verily will be the doom of hell, and theirs the doom of burning

7:155.ar: وَٱخۡتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوۡمَهُۥ سَبۡعِينَ رَجُلࣰ ا لِّمِيقَٰتِنَاۖ فَلَمَّآ أَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلرَّجۡفَةُ قَالَ رَبِّ لَوۡ شِئۡتَ أَهۡلَكۡتَهُم مِّن قَبۡلُ وَإِيَّٰيَۖ أَتُهۡلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَّآۖ إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتۡنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِهَا مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَهۡدِي مَن تَشَآءُۖ أَنتَ وَلِيُّنَا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَاۖ وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡغَٰفِرِينَ
7:155.en: And Moses chose of his people seventy men for Our appointed tryst and, when the trembling came on them, he said: My Lord! If Thou hadst willed Thou hadst destroyed them long before, and me with them. Wilt thou destroy us for that which the ignorant among us did? It is but Thy trial (of us). Thou sendest whom Thou wilt astray and guidest whom Thou wilt: Thou art our Protecting Friend, therefore forgive us and have mercy on us, Thou, the Best of all who show forgiveness

2:55.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى ٱللَّهَ جَهۡرَةࣰ فَأَخَذَتۡكُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
2:55.en: And when ye said: O Moses! We will not believe in thee till we see Allah plainly; and even while ye gazed the lightning seized you

2:56.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَٰكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَوۡتِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:56.en: Then We revived you after your extinction, that ye might give thanks

4:165.ar: رُّسُلࣰ ا مُّبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ حُجَّةُۢ بَعۡدَ ٱلرُّسُلِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:165.en: Messengers of good cheer and of warning, in order that mankind might have no argument against Allah after the messengers. Allah was ever Mighty, Wise

9:128.ar: لَقَدۡ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولࣱ مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيۡهِ مَا عَنِتُّمۡ حَرِيصٌ عَلَيۡكُم بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
