RH0f_499glg.title: Arabic Tafsir of Surat al-Qasas: 'You Were Not There', Verses 44-50
RH0f_499glg.one_line: Four times the Prophet is told 'you were not there': judge deeds not people, learn from stories, convey wisely, and the Quran suffices as proof.
RH0f_499glg.summary: The sheikh restates the surah's lessons about other people's stories: we cannot judge people from what we see, their stories are driven by simple human needs, and the point is to draw a lesson for ourselves. Verses 44-46 repeat 'you were not there' four times, at the western side, in Madyan, and at the mountain, teaching even the Prophet not to judge Musa's fleeing, Shuayb's daughters at the well, or the seventy who asked to see Allah. He backs this with Hudhayfah rebuking those who claimed they would have carried the Prophet at the Trench, and al-Miqdad warning that some who saw the Prophet are in the fire. The key distinction is between condemning a wrong act, which stays wrong and may be punished, and condemning the person. Good opinion of people is the default outside marriage, business, war and those you are raising. Verses 46-47 show messengers remove every excuse, so Muslims must convey Islam clearly and in a way people can hear: a survey found religious people themselves drive others away most, and he tells of a village preacher whose sound but ill-chosen hadith nearly got him expelled. Verses 48-50 answer the demand for Musa-like miracles: the Quran itself is the challenge and it suffices.

outline.heading: We cannot judge people from the stories we see
outline.gist: We know each other only as short stories; Musa's mother, Musa striking the man and the two women at the well would all be misjudged.

outline.heading: People's stories are simple at their core
outline.gist: Fear, vanity, pride, greed and desire drive them, yet even so we have no right to reduce someone to a bad motive.

outline.heading: Not at the western side: do not judge Musa's fleeing
outline.gist: Seeing Musa run from the staff after hearing 'I am Allah', one might think one would have done better; the verse teaches that you cannot judge a moment you did not witness.

outline.heading: Hudhayfah: 'you say what you do not know'
outline.gist: He recounted the freezing, starving night of the Trench when no one volunteered, and rebuked students who said they would have carried the Prophet on their necks.

outline.heading: Al-Miqdad: do not wish for a scene Allah spared you
outline.gist: Some who saw the Prophet with their own eyes are in the fire; be grateful you were born knowing only your Lord.

outline.heading: Judge the act, not the person
outline.gist: A deed can be named wrong, stopped and punished, but placing yourself above the doer is forbidden, as in the hadith about Yunus.

outline.heading: Study the causes instead of insulting people
outline.gist: Instead of sneering that a people deserves only military boots, find why a behaviour spread and fix it; Musa did not let one troublesome follower turn him against his people.

outline.heading: The real use of stories: take a lesson for yourself
outline.gist: Every story of success or failure holds a lesson so you need not walk the same road; reading stories only to judge wastes them.

outline.heading: Good opinion is the default, except in four cases
outline.gist: Suspicion is allowed for a marriage suitor, a business partner, an enemy in war and someone you are responsible for raising or teaching; otherwise assume the best.

outline.heading: Recitation: 'we produced generations' to 'that they may remember'
outline.gist: He recites the passage before explaining it.

outline.heading: Not a witness to Musa asking for Harun
outline.gist: Musa voiced his fear and asked for a partner prophet, which the Prophet never did; you were not there to judge whether it was fitting.

outline.heading: Long ages made Bani Israil forget, and this ummah may too
outline.gist: Do not judge them for losing their teachings; after 1,400 years your ummah may hold the Book in name only, as the hadith of following those before you warns.

outline.heading: A warning, not a fixed prophecy
outline.gist: Like warning a son where his path leads; Quraysh had lost Ibrahim's way, while people of the Book should have done better, yet Muslims could end up worse.

outline.heading: Not dwelling in Madyan: Shuayb's situation
outline.gist: One might ask why a prophet's daughters were watering flocks; you do not know his circumstances among his people.

outline.heading: Not at the mountain: the seventy who demanded to see Allah
outline.gist: One might wonder why Musa chose such men; the repeated 'you were not' leaves no other reading.

outline.heading: An error stays an error: 'he did wrong' is not 'he is bad'
outline.gist: Not knowing someone's circumstances does not make theft right; the Prophet instead said Musa was harmed more than this and was patient.

outline.heading: Condemn the sin, leave the sinner to Allah
outline.gist: If the Prophet is taught this, we more so; the adulterer is punished but not declared unforgivable, and even those who burned the believers were offered repentance.

outline.heading: A mercy from your Lord to warn a people with no prior warner
outline.gist: The Quran is your task; the people meant are Quraysh, since the Arabs had earlier prophets such as Ismail, Hud, Salih and Shuayb.

outline.heading: Recitation: the excuse and the demand for Musa's signs
outline.gist: He flags the word 'remember' for later and notes the readings sihran and sahiran.

outline.heading: Focus on your own task, not on people's faults
outline.gist: Whoever is busy with what Allah charged him with has no time for people's mistakes and honour; idle people fill their days with gossip.

outline.heading: Messengers remove every excuse
outline.gist: So that, when punished, they cannot say 'if only You had sent us a messenger'.

outline.heading: No excuse after the messengers; the people of the gap
outline.gist: Those never reached, or reached with a distorted message, are excused; the Muslims' great task is clear, correct conveying.

outline.heading: Religious people drive others from the deen
outline.gist: A survey of about 600 American Muslims found the top cause of distance from religion was religious people themselves; some would serve dawah best by silence.

outline.heading: A caller must know the people's language and culture
outline.gist: The Prophet was sent from among the Arabs, in their tongue and culture; the sheikh would not do dawah in China because he does not know its people.

outline.heading: The village preacher: true words for the wrong audience
outline.gist: A gentle, learned preacher from Homs told hardy mountain villagers of Umm Ayman drinking from the Prophet's vessel and nearly lost his post.

outline.heading: Dawah has many forms; speech needs qualifications
outline.gist: The Prophet lacked nothing for his mission; dawah through wealth, character and action is open to all, but speaking requires knowledge.

outline.heading: 'Why was he not given what Musa was given?'
outline.gist: Signs that are demanded and then rejected bring punishment, as with Pharaoh and Thamud's she-camel.

outline.heading: Addressed to Quraysh; 'two sorceries backing each other'
outline.gist: He prefers that the verse addresses Quraysh rather than the Jews; tazahara means became manifest, and they rejected both messages.

outline.heading: Recitation: bring a better book
outline.gist: He recites the passage before explaining it.

outline.heading: The Quran as the challenge
outline.gist: Allah made the Book itself the Prophet's challenge to Quraysh: bring one more guiding than the Torah and the Quran and I will follow it.

outline.heading: Musa's signs did not secure faith; do not compare your lot
outline.gist: Pharaoh and the Copts did not believe and Bani Israil worshipped the calf; comparing what others were given is another form of judging and an excuse for failure.

outline.heading: Miracle versus proofs of prophethood
outline.gist: A miracle is a sign used repeatedly to challenge; the splitting moon and multiplied food are authentic proofs of prophethood, as al-Bayhaqi termed them, not miracles.

outline.heading: The Quran's escalating challenge and its sufficiency
outline.gist: A book, a discourse, ten surahs, one surah: they failed; giving Musa-like signs would have implied the Quran was not enough.

outline.heading: Only Allah tells us people's inner states
outline.gist: Allah reassures the Prophet that those who rejected him follow their desires, so he would not blame himself; we have no such knowledge.
